human_tolerance.notes: Uses suburban lawns and gardens while foraging for soil and leaf-litter invertebrates; frequent road mortality is a conspicuous risk during range expansion.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Mating takes place during a two-to-three month season around July-August.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Young are born in March after delayed implantation, nurse for about three months, and may stay with the mother until six months to one year old.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Mating in summer; delayed implantation, young born in spring.

vocalizations.description: Low grunting and squealing, mostly between a mother and her young.
High-pitched squeal given when the animal is handled or threatened.

taxonomy.note: GBIF's backbone still lists usageKey 2440779 as Dasypus novemcinctus, while iNaturalist and the 2024 Systematic Biology revision summarized by Wikipedia split the northern lineage as Dasypus mexicanus; Louisiana observations sit under iNaturalist's D. mexicanus. Higher classification follows the GBIF backbone record for D. novemcinctus, which matches the iNaturalist classification for the split species.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2440779 is retained over non-backbone GBIF key 331806019 because 2440779 is the backbone-quality key and has Louisiana occurrence data; 331806019 resolves to Dasypus mexicanus in an IUCN-sourced non-backbone dataset but has zero Louisiana occurrences. Wikidata provides the QID and Mammal Diversity Database id; ITIS and NCBI searches found no Dasypus mexicanus record.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 and the iNaturalist taxon page report IUCN Least Concern for Dasypus mexicanus.

range.note: Country list follows Wikipedia's statement that the species occurs from the United States south through Costa Rica and iNaturalist's native United States checklist status. The United States is treated as native at country scale: Wikipedia describes late-19th-century natural crossing from Mexico, Florida introductions, and Late Pleistocene fossils in the southeast; Louisiana is retained inside the native US range for activity-region validation.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walks/shuffles on land, is an extensive burrower, and traverses rivers by floating or walking across the riverbed.

traits.skin.note: Outer shell is ossified dermal scutes covered by keratinized scales; schema value Shell best represents the carapace.

traits.nest_type.note: Rests and raises young in burrows; individuals can maintain up to 12 burrows.

traits.perching.note: Ground-dwelling and fossorial; not a perching animal.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg 3.4 kg, which falls in the schema's Medium range.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's adult weight range 2.7-4.1 kg.

traits.length_m.note: Typical adult length set below Wikipedia's stated maximum total length of 0.81 m; no open source in use gave a mean, so 0.70 m is an authored representative adult value.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Estimated from Wikipedia's description of burrows as roughly 20 cm wide, using tunnel width as a proxy for the low body/shoulder height needed to move through them.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia states 12-to-15-year lifespans; lower end used as typical.

traits.diet.note: Qualitative mapping from Wikipedia: chiefly ants, termites and other invertebrates; occasional amphibians, reptiles, eggs, baby mammals and carrion; less than 10% nonanimal matter including fruits and seeds. Fractions are authored to sum to 1.0.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia describes the species as solitary; group_size fixed to one adult for the simulation.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Solitary, mainly nocturnal, coming out to forage around dusk.

traits.defense.note: Wikipedia says alarmed animals flee with surprising speed and may dig in if escape fails; Flee chosen as the schema's primary response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a suburban, nocturnal forager that often occurs near people but usually flees or digs in when alarmed.

habitat.use.note: Judgement split for a ground-foraging animal that also rests, shelters and raises young in burrows.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Sleeps and nests in an underground burrow.

habitat.resources.note: Resource tags map the diet and shelter text to schema resources. The invertebrate tag is included and used by behavior.params.food_tag; leaf_litter marks the soil/litter foraging substrate. Weights are authored from qualitative diet proportions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement from the species being well established across the southern US, using corridors such as roads and railroads, foraging in open habitats, and suffering high roadkill.

seasonal.strategy.note: Active year-round because the species cannot hibernate and northern spread is limited by harsh winters.

seasonal.phases.note: Mating, delayed implantation, March births, nursing, juvenile association and annual reproduction timings from Wikipedia's Reproduction section.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration set to 365 days from Wikipedia statements that young leave after six months to one year and reach sexual maturity at one year; scale is authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for shared fsm-ground-forager-v1. food_tag matches habitat.resources[].tag=invertebrate; nocturnal rest_sun_lo_deg/rest_sun_hi_deg keep rest during daylight; distances and walk gait are judgement for a slow, low armadillo.

vocalizations.note: No vocalization is modeled because the open sources used here did not give a recurring, display-relevant call with timing details.

look.note: Judgement for a low blocky quadruped: elongated armored torso, short legs, long snout, small ears, tapered tail and gray-brown carapace/underside colors from Wikipedia's description. Only quadruped body-plan parts are used; poses are idle, walk and swim.

traits.home_range_ha.note: PanTHERIA HomeRange_Indiv_km2 ~0.12 km2 converted to hectares.
